Approve an increase of $1,021,000 to the cost contingency and 90 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. HH-1017, Warnerville Substation Rehabilitation – Phase 2, with Big Valley Electric, for a revised contract cost limit of $8,385,500 and a revised contract duration limit of 696 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and eleven months). This additional contingency is needed to address owner-requested changes, compliance with updated safety and regulatory requirements, hazardous materials abatement, and compatibility with Pacific Gas & Electric Company standards

Award Contract No. WD-2885, 8-Inch Ductile Iron Water Main Replacement, Sewer Replacement, and Paving Renovation on Fulton Street from Great Highway to 31st Avenue and on Various Side Streets, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, KJ Woods Construction, Inc., in the amount of $9,888,000 and with a duration of 630 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and eight months), to install water mains and sewer lines in the Outer Richmond neighborhood of San Francisco. The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), and the Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the CEQA pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code Section 31.04(h)

Approve Amendment No. 1 to Contract No. CS-1248, Equipment and Software Maintenance, with Schneider Electric Systems USA, Inc., increasing the contract amount by $5,352,254, and increasing the contract duration by five years, for a total not-to-exceed contract amount of $6,897,586, and a total contract duration of eight years, due to ongoing maintenance that is needed for the existing Wastewater Enterprise distributed control system
Update on General Manager selection process
items.text: Update on General Manager selection process. (Discussion only) President Arce thanked Commissioner Stacy for her role, expertise, and experience representing the Commission to recruit the next SFPUC General Manager (GM) and asked Commissioner Stacy for an update. Commissioner Stacy reported that the San Francisco Department of Human Resources (DHR) selected CPS Human Resources Consulting Services from the City’s list of qualified consultants and the contract was finalized on August 26, 2026. The plan is for CPS to post the job listing within the next few days and Commissioner Stacy thanked Mr. Sherburne (Assistant Director, Employment Services) and Mr. Bito (Human Resources Manager, Employment Services) for their assistance, support, and expertise. Commissioner Stacy stated the Commission seeks as much input as possible from members of the public and employees and explained there will be two separate surveys posted, one on the SFPUC website for the public and a second posted internally for SFPUC employee access. Commissioner Stacy encouraged feedback anytime the GM selection process is agendized to help inform priorities and named the Citizens’ Advisory Committee (CAC) hoping they include the GM selection as a future agenda discussion item and the Commissioner also encouraged feedback from BAWSCA, and other stakeholders. The Commissioner stated the résumé submittal date is October 16 th if everything goes according to plan and the Commissioner review will commence shortly the

items.text: Public Hearing to consider possible action to approve: 1) the proposed “Electric Schedule NBT-CleanPowerSF, Net Billing Tariff” (CleanPowerSF Net Billing Tariff) and 2) a revised “Electric Schedule NEM-CleanPowerSF, Net Energy Metering” (NEM Tariff) both to be effective the first day of the May 2027 billing period. items.text: Award Contract No. WW-770, Oceanside Water Pollution Control Plant HVAC Upgrades, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Monterey Mechanical Co., in the amount of $22,309,000 and with a duration of 790 consecutive calendar days (approximately two years and two months), to upgrade ventilation systems of several structures on site.
